req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. Tests must cover: (1) positive — a valid existing post id returns non-404 for update/delete; (2) negative — a clearly non-existent id returns exactly 404; (3) boundary — id just beyond the highest existing post (id=21) returns 404; additional cases cover both HTTP methods (GET and POST) for update, and POST for delete, plus id=0 as a boundary below the minimum valid id. All tests log in as a user who owns posts to avoid 403 masking 404. Mutation resilience: exact status code assertions (catches 404->403, 404->400, 404->200 mutations), both update and delete endpoints tested, boundary ±1 around max post id (20).

tests.name: test_update_existing_post_returns_200
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with 20 posts; post id=2 authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone)
User Rahul is logged in
expected: HTTP 200 — post exists, author matches, update form rendered
trace: R-FLASKR-022: existing post must NOT return 404
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_existing_post_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200

test_update_existing_post_returns_200()
